Estimate the equation of the trend line for the scatter plot above. Round both the slope and the $y$-intercept to the nearest $0.5.$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14224903/assets/fd3ce3de75fa9296c721e3f3a28bef241eae6350819c4cc7a54707921c0c1fe4.png)

It seems that the trend line passes through $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})≈(2,7)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})≈(8,4).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we estimate the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ≈\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{4-7}{8-2} \\  & =\frac{-3}{6} \\  & =-0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-0.5$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-0.5x+b.
$$

We now need to estimate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,7):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-0.5x+b \\ 7 & =-0.5(2)+b \\ 7 & =-1+b \\ 8 & =b \\ b & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-0.5x+8.
$$
